title: Patti close
hook: a wedding song remembered long after a grocery list: closing the Patti, an alphabet set in a raga and signed by Nanak the poet

segments.voice: Yesterday, the scholar's mistake: thinking reading is the finish line. Your line was live the letters. Where did your one word show up, out in the open? Day one thousand one hundred fifty-eight.

A grocery list is gone from memory by the weekend. A song heard once at a cousin's wedding comes back years later with every word in place, because the tune held on to them. For four days this path has read the Patti as a tablet, as letters, as a lesson. It was always a song as well, with a raga to carry it. Today we close it, and listen to it that way.
screen: `THE FAST MIDDLE PART.` → `THE TUNE CARRIES THE LETTERS.` → `THE PATTI AS A SONG.`

segments.voice: First, where it lives. The Patti doesn't sit in the Guru Granth Sahib as a school primer. It's placed in Raga Asa, among hymns that are sung. Its heading gives it a raga, which tells a musician how to sing it. The alphabet comes with a tune attached. Second, its refrain. The Rahao, the line we spent two days with, is the center the song keeps coming back to: why do you forget, foolish mind? When you give your account, then you'll be counted educated. Letter after letter moves forward, and the refrain pulls the mind back. That's how a song teaches. Third, how it ends. The last stanza says, in paraphrase: the One who made everything is doing all that is done, makes it happen, and knows it all. Thus says Nanak the poet. Saair, poet. Guru Nanak signs his alphabet not as a schoolmaster but as a poet. The Patti ends as a poem that knows it's a poem. Fourth, look at what the song carried these last days. The tablet, and learning one mark at a time. Sasai, the made world and one Master of all. The letters of the mind: gray hair, blame, and the show we put on. And the scholar's mistake: the real exam is a life. Read those as a list and they're a lot. Sung, they're one thing: an alphabet turned toward God, with a tune to carry it until the heart can hold it alone. That's why the close is a song. Today's line: the alphabet sings.
screen: `SET IN RAGA ASA.` · `THE RAHAO PULLS THE MIND BACK.` · `THUS SAYS NANAK THE POET.` · `ONE ALPHABET, TURNED TOWARD GOD.` · then, large: `THE ALPHABET SINGS.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: sing one letter's line. Choose one from the Patti: sasai, the One who made the world is Master of all; or dadai, I blame no one, the fault is in my deeds. If you can, find a recording of the Patti in Raga Asa and listen for your letter. If not, hum the line softly to any simple tune that comes, even two notes going up and down. Sing it, or hum it, three or four times. Then let it go quiet and sit with whatever stays. If you pray, you can end with Waheguru. The bell holds the time.
Patti close. Guru Nanak's alphabet, set in Raga Asa, carried by a refrain to the mind, and signed: thus says Nanak the poet. Today's word.
Your line: the alphabet sings. Today, hum your one letter's line while you walk or wash up, and let the tune carry it for you. Day one thousand one hundred fifty-eight.

howItsDone: Ragis sing the Patti in Raga Asa as kirtan, returning to the Rahao line between stanzas, and some sangats sing it with children learning Gurmukhi so the letters and their meanings are learned together.
